title: Introduce SparkPipe attention kernel and fused-rotary picker with continuous-batching hints
author: Maya Patel
ci_checks: cuda-integration: fail on first run (OOM on ci-nvidia-rt-3) -> fixed memory fencing -> rerun -> pass
description: Context: Attention kernel performance remains the dominant cost for many inference workloads. Previous optimizations focused on microkernel improvements and rotary/rope fusion, but we still see suboptimal behavior when the runtime switches between kernel variants at request time and when KV layout causes fragmentation under continuous batching. Motivation: ship a compact, hardware-friendly attention path that (a) reduces kernel-selection jitter, (b) packs KV caches into a fused layout to lower memory and warmup overhead, and (c) surfaces lightweight hints to the continuous-batcher to improve steady-state throughput. Change summary: 1) Add SparkPipe attention microkernel: a tiled, register-first microkernel optimized for 16/8-bit matmul with prefetch-friendly stride. 2) Implement a fused-rotary "picker": a kernel-selector that precomputes a minimal metadata fingerprint (sequence-length bucket, head-size, quantized-layout) to choose between SparkPipe, HW-Optimized, and LegacyFlash variants without running probing kernels. 3) Introduce a KV fused layout in runtime/caches that stores rotary coefficients adjacent to QKV memory to enable single-pass preheat and decrease KV pointer chasing. 4) Add continuous-batcher hints (runtime/batcher/hints.go) so the scheduler can group requests by picker-key to reduce kernel-switching and improve batching efficiency. 5) Provide a feature-flag and rollout plan: sparkpipe.enabled flag, per-customer rollout control, and automatic fallback to legacy kernels when memory pressure is detected. Benchmarks (summary): On A100-like hw and our micro-bench harness with mixed sequence lengths, we measured p50 latency -14% on short sequences (<=64), p99 -21% on mixed sequences, and end-to-end throughput +28% for steady, batched chat workloads. KV memory consumption reduced ~18% for typical 8-bit QKV workloads due to fused layout. Design notes: - Picker generates a 16-bit key derived from {seq_bucket, head_dim_bucket, quant_bitflag, rotary-mode} and is designed to be cheap to compute (single cmp/shift sequence). - SparkPipe keeps a fastpath for in-register rotary application to amortize rotary math across heads. - Continuous-batcher hint is advisory; scheduler still maintains latency SLOs and can preempt groupings. Testing & validation: unit tests for kernel math and picker; integration tests against runtime with synthetic workloads; full CI benchmark run; manual validation on Dedicated pools. Rollout: staged canary at 5% customers -> 25% -> 100% with automated metric guardrails (latency, error-rate, KV-evictions). Backward compat: no API changes; runtime falls back to legacy kernels when the picker key isn't supported or when memory safety checks fail. Follow-ups: follow-up tasks to extend picker for heterogeneous GPU fleets (ENG-3381) and to instrument picker telemetry for better model selection heuristics.

kv-memory: -18% for 8-bit QKV when using fused layout
continuous-batcher effectiveness: kernel-switch rate down 3.6x when hints enabled
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: sparkpipe.enabled (default off in prod). To enable for a tenant use the Console rollout UI or feature API.
Telemetry: picker.selected_variant and picker.key are emitted to runtime telemetry; add to per-tenant dashboards.
Rollback: set sparkpipe.enabled=false or use runtime/attn/variants_registry.go to force legacy
Known issue: initial CI run OOM on older CI nodes; fixed with memory fence but ops should monitor GPU memory regressions during canary
